Also: "Proactive Monte Carlo simulations ... indicated that a sample size of 220 would be sufficient for this analysis (our n = 475)."

section_summary.extract_value: This analytic strategy describes a two-step EFA-to-CFA approach applied to Malay and Chinese participants: the Malay sample was split into two halves (EFA: women n = 149, men n = 157; CFA: Malay women n = 121, Malay men n = 114) and the CFA half was combined with Chinese participants (women n = 120, men n = 120) yielding n = 475 for CFA. Missing data (1.1%) were multiply imputed; EFA was conducted separately by sex and CFA used robust maximum likelihood with Satorra-Bentler correction, plus tests of measurement invariance and assessments of reliability and convergent/incremental validity.
section_summary.evidence_source: Quoted sentences: "Thus, the Malay sample was first split ... resulting in one split-half for EFA (women n = 149, men n = 157) and a second split-half for CFA (Malay women n = 121, Malay men n = 114); the latter was combined with data from Chinese participants (women n = 120, men n = 120)." and "Proactive Monte Carlo simulations ... indicated that a sample size of 220 would be sufficient for this analysis (our n = 475)." Also: "Missing data ... made up only 1.1% of the total dataset, so we imputed these individual missing data points using the multiple imputation technique."
